newsitem.title: USA: Boston Beer Co CEO sees sector shakeout.
newsitem.headline: Boston Beer Co CEO sees sector shakeout.

text.p: Tough times are brewing for craft brewers, Boston Beer Co's chief executive officer told shareholders at the company's annual meeting on Tuesday.

"We're entering a period of consolidation, retrenchment and eventually a shakeout," Jim Koch told the shareholders, explaining that the number of competitors in the craft brewing market had doubled since 1995 to 400.

"There's not room in the marketplace" for all those beers, he said, noting that Boston Beer, the maker of Sam Adams, was the only one of the seven U.S. publicly traded craft brewers to show a profit in the first quarter of 1997.

Koch warned shareholders that last year's 26 percent increase in sales, marking the first time since Prohibition that a new American brewery had produced over one million barrels of beer, would probably not be repeated in 1997.
The first quarter of 1997 showed Boston Beer with 4.0 percent sales growth.

Koch said he expected to see "more price pressures and aggressiveness" from competitors but intended to compete by maintaining Boston Beer "as a lean, entrepreneurial company. We don't spend any money we don't need to.
"But we're not going to change the beer or our core values," he said. "Those are to brew the best beer we can and give it to people fresh."

The company will be phasing out its Long Shot line, three beers that won its homebrew contest from more than 1,600 entries. Citing the number of new mircro and craft brews in the market, Koch said he decided to end the public distribution of those beers, though not the contest.

Boston Beer will only be introducing one new product in the United States this summer -- Boston Cream Ale -- now available in the United Kingdom as the result of a partnership with Whitbread Plc. The brew, an amber ale, is quite successful in the United Kingdom, where it was introduced in 1996, Koch said. "We (the partnership) expect to make several hundred thousands barrels over there," he said.
